name: Module 1b: cell prep (demo scale, simulated)
description: DEMO SCALE: 30 x 20 mm, one fluidic layer at ONE depth (0.3 mm: every chamber and channel), resin print + hot emboss. Channels are 0.2 mm wide (clamped up to the 0.2 mm open-channel floor), the quench mixer is a folded 0.2 mm channel with 0.4 mm walls, ports are 800 um at >= 5 mm pitch (6 of 6), and every chamber and channel names its CAD block (contracts/blocks.json). RETENTION: the cell filter is a depth weir (block trap_chamber): a 273 um tall x 200 um thick crest leaves a 27 um gap under the lid, printable because the 200 um floor limits width, not z; it strains clumps from about 80 um and single cells pass. THAT RETENTION IS DERIVED FROM THE GAP: a 27 um gap holds a clump of 68-90 um and upwards by the band in contracts/blocks.json, so retains_um is 80, the middle of it. The brief's 30-40 um clumps are NOT caught and cannot be: they would need a 9-12 um gap, and at the +/-20 um z tolerance of a weir that target could come out negative. All of that is DATA on m1b_filter_1.retention (crest_height_um, crest_thickness_um, opening_um, retains_um), and filter.gap_um is the same gap, not a second one. There is no mesh. MIXING IS ADVECTIVE: both mixers are herringbone_mixer blocks (chevron relief in the same layer), because a plain fold or a wide chamber does not mix at Re far below 1. The cell wash is a spiral_channel used as a long co-flow path, which is slow and incomplete but is a named method: a DLD array cannot sort cells at the 200 um floor (critical diameter about 105 um) and inertial focusing needs flows far above the cell-safe shear limit. Automated bridge from Module 1 to Module 2: quench (T-junction + herringbone), wash, filter, count at a QC window, resuspend in dextran buffer, send to Module 2's core inlet. Designed and simulated; not printed this weekend. GENERATED by cad/generators/m1b_cellprep.py.

module.name: Cell prep (draft)
module.note: Superseded by cell_prep_v1, which is the chip that does THIS job - detach, quench, count - and which protocols/pipeline_mvp.json runs as the cellprep module. This used to point at module1_v1, the culture chip: module 1 grows the cells and ends with its own dissociation, but it is not the successor to a cell-prep board, and naming it here sent anyone following the trail to the wrong file. Kept for reference, out of the pipeline.

chambers.note: Quench: the quench medium joins at a T-junction, then a HERRINGBONE MIXER mixes it in. Mixing has to be ADVECTIVE: at Re far below 1 a plain serpentine fold only stacks the two streams side by side and leaves diffusion to do the work, so the chevrons (relief inside the one 0.3 mm layer, like the weir crest) drive chaotic advection instead. The folded path gives the length: 6 turns, 36.3 mm of 0.2 mm channel with 0.4 mm walls. The cross-section is unchanged, so the shear-limited flow is the same as for a plain fold.

Cell wash: a SPIRAL CHANNEL used as a LONG PATH (blocks.json spiral_channel: 'inertial focusing or long path'), with clean buffer co-flowed from m1b_wash_in_1 and the old liquid taken off at m1b_waste_1. The method is named, not TBC, and the two methods it is not are ruled out on numbers: NOT a dld_array, because at the 200 um in-plane floor the DLD critical diameter is about 105 um, five times a 10-20 um cell; and NOT inertial focusing in this spiral, because the Reynolds number at the cell-safe shear-limited flow below is orders of magnitude too low. Exchange here is co-flow plus diffusion across the lane, so it is slow and incomplete: that is the honest limit of this stage.

Clump filter: a DEPTH WEIR, a 273 um tall x 200 um thick crest across the chamber leaves a 27 um gap under the lid (z only: the 200 um floor limits width, not height). Single cells of 10-20 um pass under it and clumps from about 80 um stay behind. THAT 80 um IS DERIVED FROM THE 27 um GAP, NOT CHOSEN: the retention rule in contracts/blocks.json holds a particle only while the gap is at or above gap_factor_low x its diameter and strictly below gap_factor_high x it, which for a 27 um gap puts the smallest retained clump in 68-90 um; 80 um is the middle of that, so the +/-20 um z tolerance on the gap has the most room on either side. WHAT IT DOES NOT CATCH: the design brief wanted 30-40 um clumps stopped, and this weir does not stop them. A 30 um clump needs a 9-12 um gap, which is undeliverable here: the gap is a Z dimension at +/-20 um, so a 12 um target could come out at zero or negative and seal the chamber shut. The gap stays at the buildable end and this field says what that buys instead of what was asked for. ONE gap, ONE number: retention.opening_um and filter.gap_um are the same value, and the crest is carried as data (retention.crest_height_um = this chip's etch depth minus the gap, crest_thickness_um, retains_um), so it can be machined from the spec. Untested: z tolerance is a large fraction of a gap this small, so run a coupon first.
Optical window: a counter reads cell concentration and viability (simulated: operator/cellprep.py).

Wide (1.5 mm), short HERRINGBONE MIXER: resuspends the cells in dextran buffer at the dilution the operator sets. Wide and short keeps the pressure drop low in a viscous buffer, but a plain wide chamber does not mix at Re far below 1 - it just carries the two liquids side by side - so the floor carries chevron relief (same layer, same etch depth) for chaotic advection. The cross-section is unchanged, so the shear-limited flow is still set by the width.
